register: The sources an application may ask the frame to fetch
note: QGD-APP-0008. An application names a source; the URL is here. It never names a destination and never opens a connection — the fetch is the Rust credential core's, because all of this product's outbound HTTPS goes through it (D-18, D-31). A grant is source:<id>, so adding a source means adding its grant to data/extension-grants.json as well, and an application asking for a source with no grant is refused before the URL is looked up.

politeness.note: #79, KI7MT 2026-10-26: no source is asked more often than this, whatever a manifest or Refresh asks. The credential core enforces it: this file is compiled into it, so nothing outside that process can loosen it. Where a provider states a limit, that limit; where none is stated, our judgement and the reason, so it can be revisited (CLAUDE.md, security.md: rate limiting).

solar.basis: NOAA SWPC states no limit. The observed solar-cycle indices are a monthly product: more than once a day learns nothing.

noaa-flux.basis: NOAA SWPC states no limit. The 10.7 cm flux summary changes a few times a day; 15 minutes is the Conditions page's own cadence.

noaa-kp.basis: NOAA SWPC states no limit. Kp is a 3-hour index; 15 minutes is the Conditions page's own cadence.

noaa-scales.basis: NOAA SWPC states no limit. The R/S/G scales follow the same observations; 15 minutes, the Conditions page's cadence.

pota-spots.basis: POTA's API is unofficial and undocumented; its volunteers ask users not to hammer it. Spots change by the minute, so once a minute, the same as qso-graph's pota-mcp.
